title: Counting closed-system kits against the HMO straight-tip limit: Urology and Continence Supply Program
content:
On the Continence Commercial HMO Program of the Urology and Continence Supply Program, the plan counts closed-system catheter kits (A4353) against the same monthly limit as straight-tip intermittent catheters (A4351). When a straight-tip refill's charge is settled, kit units are therefore added to the refill's units in its excess over the limit.

## How kits are added

1. When closed-system catheter kits shipped on the program within the last 3 calendar months, the newest kit order's quantity per 30 days, taken for the refill's supply days, is added to the refill's units in its excess over the limit.
2. When kits shipped within the last 12 calendar months but none within the last 3, one twelfth of the kit units shipped in those 12 months, rounded down, per 30 days, is added instead.
3. Otherwise nothing is added.

The newest kit order is the closed-system kit (A4353) written order with the latest order date. A kit shipment is within the last 3 calendar months when it is dated fewer than 3 whole calendar months before the date the charge is settled. The 12-month window is read the same way.

## Examples (hypothetical; a 30-day refill)

| Kit history | Newest kit order | Kit units added per 30 days |
|---|---|---|
| a kit refill 2 months ago | 40 per 30 days | 40 |
| none in the last 3 months; 130 kit units in the last 12 | any | 10, because 130 divided by 12 is 10.83, rounded down |
| none in the last 12 months | any | none |

For a 60-day refill, the first row adds 40 for each 30 days, which is 80.
